question: In plain SPHEREx photos, with nothing subtracted, is there a point of light where JPL Horizons puts Pluto, and is that place empty in a same-colour photo from another visit?
written: 2026-11-15T12:11+00:00, after the difference test of pluto_rule.json had failed and before any plain photo was measured for this test
why_a_second_rule: The first rule (pluto_rule.json) looked for Pluto in the difference of two photos. Most of its misses were a stronger peak elsewhere in the search box, left by stars that the difference does not cancel; the check of differences (K8) failed for the same reason. This rule asks the question the way a blink comparator answers it: a light at the predicted place in one photo, and nothing at that place in the other. The first rule's FAIL stays on the Checks page beside this one.
positions: JPL Horizons, observer SPHEREx (id -163182), astrometric ICRS, target 999 (Pluto), at the mid-exposure time of every photo (as in pluto_rule.json)
pairs: the same photos and twins as pluto_rule.json: the frames that hold Pluto at least 12 pixels from the detector edge, each with its same-colour twin from another visit (the shared match rule; a twin is dropped when Pluto is within 12 pixels of that position at the twin's time), at most 24 pairs per detector, evenly spaced in time
photo: the photo's stamp, 48 by 48 pixels centred on Pluto's predicted place, its background removed (sigma-clipped median), smoothed with a Gaussian of 1 pixel; heights are in units of the robust noise of the smoothed stamp itself
twin: the twin's stamp at the same sky position, resampled onto the photo's pixels, its background removed, smoothed and scaled the same way
found: in the smoothed photo the brightest pixel within 1.5 pixels of the predicted place is at least 5 noise units high, and a round Gaussian fitted to the unsmoothed photo there has its centre within 1 pixel (6.15 arcsec) of the predicted place
empty: in the smoothed twin no pixel within 1 pixel of that fitted centre reaches 3 noise units
per_detector: each detector is judged on its own; a detector with fewer than 4 pairs is not judged
passes_if: in at least one detector at least 80 percent of the pairs are both found and empty
if_it_passes: a showcase of the passing detector with the most pairs (ties: the lower detector): its photos with a ring where Horizons puts Pluto, position only, no spectrum and no label of any ice
if_it_fails: no Pluto showcase; the row says FAIL
